text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An informal moratorium on military overflights in Cyprus goes up in smoke after Turkey's violations of Cypriot airspace yesterday, but Cyprus will stick to the committment it made to the United States to suspend Greek overflights.
- Communust Akel is peeved at the apparent deadlock in talks with other opposition parties to find a presidential candidate.
- An 18-year-old on his first day at work was killed yesterday when a huge metal drum fell on him.
- Cyprus protests at Turkish air violations.
- Attorney-General Alecos Markides has turned down a request to disband the Cyprus Motorcyclists Association following last month's riots in Nicosia after a United Nations peace concert.
- Insurance company Eurolife claims a first with the launch of its Euroline service.
- An error has been spotted on the new one pound notes, with a mix-up in the name of the village depicted on the note.
- Fifteen Cypriot companies will take part in a trade delegation to Israel this weekend.
- Communist Akel party leader Demetris Christofias dismisses speculation that the name of politician Tassos Papadopoulos was put forward as a presidential candidate in discussions with other parties.

- Britain's Sir David Hannay arrives in Cyprus next week with clear ideas and proposals on the basic aspects of the Cyprus problem for talks with President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash ahead of direct talks scheduled for July.
- Police know who pulled the trigger in the attempted murder of a Larnaca gambling club owner last week.
- For the past 10 days Cyprus's airspace has been continuously violated by Turkish and Israeli warplanes.
